transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-15 14:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Ortega (Redwood SE), Arjun Mehta (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (Head of ML, StratusRetail), Evan Brooks (Platform Eng), Sanjay Patel (Security), Lina Gomez (Product)

Summary: quick check on access handoff, run results, and next-step bench runs; some mis-keys in the staging IAM but otherwise moving.

[00:00] Maya: alright hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick 40 minute sync, cover infra status, quick bench recap, and then action items. Priya, Evan, can you confirm we're still on for VPC peering today?
[00:12] Priya: yes we're on, Evan's pulled the request and the network team is lookin at it. should be approved before tomorrow noon, knock on wood.
[00:20] Evan: yah we filed the peering, just need the route propagation and a small firewall egress allow. i'll share the ip ranges after this call.
[00:28] Lucas: great, that'll unblock us for the staging runs. quick note on the creds - we saw the service account token expired in the first job, arjun got a new one?
[00:36] Arjun: yeah i reissued the token and updated the terraform var in the onboarding repo, should be good but i did see a permission gap for the gateway route table which we flagged.
[00:45] Maya: ok good. we scheduled today's micro-bench - lucas take us through the headline numbers?
[00:52] Lucas: sure; ran two profiles on staging - default fp16 pipeline and a quant-4 profile. sequences at 256 tokens, steady concurrency at 4, ran prefix cache and no-cache runs. fp16 median p50 about 160ms per token, 95th was 420ms which was higher than expected, but with KV cache on the 95th dropped to ~220ms. quant-4 median 130ms, 95th about 310ms, and with KV cache it's down to 180-190ms. so overall quantization helped, but we need to watch regressions on output quality.
[01:35] Priya: ok the client product expectation is p95 under 250ms for short responses, we hit that with quant on with cache, but curious about the failure mode where cache misses spike latency.
[01:48] Lucas: cache miss spikes are a thing when prefix diversity is high – we saw it in the run around 11:12. also the KV cache warmup depending on routing split can take a few requests. we recommended a warmup traffic pattern or sticky routing.
[02:05] Priya: sticky routing meaning keep requests pinned to the same worker to utilize cache?
[02:10] Lucas: exactly, or route by conversation id. if you have multi-region traffic it's trickier.
[02:16] Evan: we mostly are single-region but will have periodic bursts from EU. does redwood have auto fallback to lower-capacity models in those events?
[02:24] Maya: yes, we can configure routing policies: prefer dedicated with fallback to hosted shared variants, and specify compatible model family for graceful degradation.
[02:31] Lina: any change to tokenization or outputs when running quant-4? we can't tolerate hallucination increase.
[02:36] Lucas: so far output fidelity with our chosen quant profile was within the eval set thresholds – about 0.8 ROUGE/whatever equivalent on their internal tests, but we should run their regression harness. quant introduces subtle changes, so plan is to run your prompt set through both fp16 and quant-4 and compare.
[02:55] Priya: we'll send a 200 prompt subset tomorrow.
[03:00] Maya: perfect. on security, sso and kms notes? Sanjay?
[03:05] Sanjay: quick flag - we need confirmation on KMS key ownership model. we prefer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for audit. does redwood support HSM or KMS integration?
[03:14] Maya: yes, private deployments and dedicated both support customer-managed KMS via our KMS integration; for hosted we also offer envelope encryption and can link to customer KMS, but full HSM-managed keys are part of the private package. we'll share the integration doc.
[03:28] Sanjay: and audit logs - we need request-level logs exported to our SIEM, retention 13 months, is that doable?
[03:35] Arjun: we can export audit events to your S3 or SIEM; retention is configurable on private/dedicated tiers, hosted has shorter default retention but we have add-on options.
[03:45] Sanjay: ok we'll map that. are there PII redaction controls?
[03:49] Lucas: we have redaction hooks and can configure pre-processing rules; also a deterministic scrub layer if you need.
[03:56] Priya: coming back to bench - any memory constraints on your staging GPUs that would cause p95 spikes?
[04:01] Lucas: staging used a single A100 equivalent pod and the KV cache size/eviction policy mattered. when we hit multi-convo with long contexts we saw OOM-ish slowdowns due to swapping – not crashes but heavy GC. we recommend either increasing the worker memory or moving to a multi-worker shard config.
[04:22] Evan: for us increasing memory is painful on cost, is there a middle ground?
[04:27] Lucas: yes option: reduce live KV retention window or use prefix-only cache for certain routes; that reduces memory without huge perf loss. also batching knobs will help with throughput but tune latency tradeoffs.
[04:40] Priya: what about response streaming? we need streaming for snappier UX. does quantization affect token-by-token streaming latency?
[04:49] Lucas: no, streaming path is the same; quant affects per-token compute but streaming chunk sizes and prefetch determine perceived latency. we can configure smaller chunk sizes for UX.
[04:58] Maya: quick check on credentials - Evan you'll drop the peering details and firewall ports; arjun said token is fixed but gateway route needs a rule, anything else?
[05:07] Evan: i'll share the ip ranges and a sample SG rule after the call.
[05:12] Arjun: also FYI the onboarding repo had outdated client cert references, i pushed an update to the docs.
[05:18] Lina: on timelines, assuming peering and bench confirmations, when could we start a pilot ramp?
[05:23] Maya: if we get peering plus bench by mid-next week we can do a staged pilot the week after. so target QA -> pilot by 2026-03-23.
[05:31] Priya: sounds good. two little asks: 1) can you provide the raw bench csvs and 2) give a short note on tradeoffs of reducing 95th via cache vs increasing dedicated capacity?
[05:41] Lucas: yes will include raw csvs and a one-pager with cost/latency tradeoffs (eg: caching reduces per-token cost but increases warmup complexity; dedicated increases baseline cost but stabilizes p95).
[05:55] Priya: also need a quick blurb for execs on why we might choose quant vs pure fp16.
[06:02] Maya: we'll whip up a short slide.
[06:06] Sanjay: back to security - if we go dedicated, we need SAML SSO integrated and SCIM for provisioning. is that on the roadmap?
[06:13] Maya: yes SAML and SCIM supported for dedicated and private; we'll share the SSO integration guide and sample metadata.
[06:20] Evan: question on fallback: if dedicated capacity is full, can requests overflow to hosted without exposing data to shared infra?
[06:28] Maya: we support routing policies; overflow can be configured to a sanitized hosted variant where payloads are redacted or sent through a VPC egress. full data isolation requires private/dedicated only. we'll note the options.
[06:40] Lucas: small note on monitoring - we'll send route-level latency dashboards and token cost breakdown for the pilot so you can watch unit economics.
[06:50] Priya: great. any blockers from your side?
[06:53] Evan: need the IP ranges and plan for firewall, otherwise no blockers.
[06:56] Sanjay: need the SOC2 doc and KMS integration details.
[07:00] Maya: will send both.
[07:03] Arjun: last technical point: can we capture example failure traces when a cache miss causes spike? i want those traces for our infra runbook.
[07:11] Lucas: yep we'll attach tracing spans and a sample flamegraph.
[07:16] Lina: ok, wrap up?
[07:18] Maya: quick recap: Redwood to send pricing/burst matrix, SSO/KMS doc, raw bench csvs and tradeoff one-pager. Customer to confirm peering and firewall rules. Lucas to run quant bench with KV cache variations and share 95p runs. Next sync same time next week unless we need earlier.
[07:34] Priya: thanks all.
[07:36] Maya: thanks team, bye.

Notes: transcription contains a few label swaps and occasional filler; product names may be slightly off in speech.
